battle.name: 第一次鴉片戰爭
battle.theater: 珠江口外海與長江下游
battle.brief: 一八三九年林則徐虎門銷煙後，英國以護商為名封鎖廣州；一八四〇年一月七日穿鼻海戰揭幕，英軍相繼攻下定海、廈門，一八四二年沿長江直抵南京，簽訂《南京條約》。卡面法軍雷管步槍與英軍一八四二年制式步槍同屬一個技術世代，但法國於本次戰爭保持中立，此槍未曾在珠江口與南京的戰場出現。

kit.name: 雷管步槍
kit.history: 雷管取代火燧之後，底火在霧裡也打得響。射程變長，隊形就散了。

countries: 交戰的兩方是清朝與大英帝國，但都不是以國家全體之力投入，而是以廣東一隅拉開的局部戰爭。清廷在戰區以廣東、廣西兩省為基地，調集兩省綠營兵與就地召集的鄉團、練勇，兵源以本省人及湖南人為主；北京由道光帝坐鎮，先後派欽差大臣琦善赴廣州議和，議和不成，改以兩江總督怡良、廣東將軍耆英主持前方軍務，兵餉轉運則由戶部、兵部在內地各省分攤。真正擋在江口的是水師與砲台：廣東水師提督關天培鎮守虎門，福建水師提督陳化成守廈門，總兵郭永陞掌沙角砲台，浙江水師提督鄭永紹守定海，鎮江由京口副都統海齡主持，福建巡撫顏伯燾在廈門城下。英方是皇家海軍遠東分艦隊與海陸混合遠征軍：海軍以七十四門的旗艦康華利號為核心，配阿克提翁號、尼米西斯號、劍橋號、焚火號等，其中尼米西斯號是鐵殼蒸汽船，能在珠江與長江逆風逆流上行；陸軍方面，除駐印度的第 68、55、71、84 團外，還有第 39 步槍旅第一營、皇家海軍陸戰隊第一營與第二營、孟加拉印度步兵第一團等印度部隊，遠征軍由海軍少將古將軍統率。商人與教士雖非交戰方，怡和洋行、威妥臣洋行等鴉片商行與各國商船、教士的安危，卻是英國開戰理由的另一半。
countriesEn: The two belligerents were the Qing court and the British Empire, but neither committed its whole strength: this was a local war fought out of the single province of Guangdong. On the Qing side the theatre was supplied from the provinces of Guangdong and Guangxi, with Green Standard troops of the two provinces reinforced by locally raised village militia and braves, most of them natives of Guangdong or of Hunan; the throne in Beijing was represented by the Daoguang Emperor, and it first sent the imperial commissioner Qishan to Canton to negotiate, and when negotiation failed replaced him with the Governor-General of Liangguang Yiliang and the Guangdong General-in-Chief Yishan, while the Ministry of Revenue and the Ministry of War apportioned pay and transport among the inland provinces. What actually stood in the way at the river mouth was the naval force and the forts: the Guangdong naval commander Guan Tianpei held Humen, the Fujian naval commander Chen Huacheng held Amoy, the brigade commander Guo Yongsheng held the Sheqiao fort, the Zhejiang naval commander Chu Yupu held Dinghai, the Jiangzhou sub-commandant Hailing held Zhenjiang, and the Fujian governor Yan Baozao was below the walls of Amoy. On the British side were the Royal Navy's China Station and a combined naval and military expedition: the navy was built around the seventy-four-gun flagship HMS Cornwallis, with HMS Actaeon, HMS Nemesis, HMS Cambridge and HMS Phlegethon; HMS Nemesis was an iron-hulled steamship able to work upstream against wind and current in the Pearl River and the Yangtze. The army brought the 68th, 55th, 71st and 84th Regiments from India, the 1st Battalion of the 39th Rifle Brigade, the 1st and 2nd Battalions of the Royal Marines, and Indian troops such as the 1st Bengal Native Infantry, the whole expedition being commanded by the naval commander-in-chief Sir Hugh Gough. Merchants and missionaries were not belligerents, but the safety of the opium houses of Jardine, Matheson and Wedderburn, and of foreign shipping, was the other half of the British case for war.
people: 決定這場戰爭走向的有兩批人。中國一方首推林則徐：他一八三九年一月到廣州，六月六日至二十五日在虎門海灘當眾銷煙，收繳英美商行鴉片二百三十七萬餘斤；整頓海防、籌措水師、搜集西方地誌與海防資料，後來成為魏源《海國圖志》的底本；一八四〇年六月他被革職戍伊犁，交戰正酣時已不在廣州。兩廣總督鄧廷楨一八三八年在黃埔絞決吸食鴉片者，與林則徐共同執行銷煙，同年病卒。琦善一八四〇年一月奉旨議和，所議條件包括割讓香港，旋遭道光帝斥責，十一月押解進京，翌年二月死於途中。耆英一八四〇年底接手廣東軍務，一八四一年一月二十六日在穿鼻大敗英軍，隨即被調離。守將之中，關天培在虎門砲台殉國，陳化成在廈門殉國，郭永陞戰死沙角，海齡在鎮江城破後自盡，鄭永紹以定海降英，顏伯燾在廈門失守後投海自盡，另有若干失地指揮官被論斬。英方主角是義律：他是駐華貿易總監，一八三九年三月致函林則徐要求交出全部鴉片，十一月下令商人武裝船隊在穿鼻攔截中國帆船，開啟穿鼻衝突；他其後在穿鼻受傷，被召回後由璞鼎查接任，璞鼎查一八四二年率軍溯長江，八月二十九日在康華利號上簽下《南京條約》。陸軍總指揮是海軍少將古，廈門之戰由科德律治指揮艦隊，年輕的戈登則隨皇家海軍陸戰隊第二營在鎮江上岸，見證了這場戰爭最慘烈的一夜。
peopleEn: Two sets of men decided the course of this war. On the Chinese side the first was Lin Zexu: he reached Canton in January 1839 and between 6 May and 25 June destroyed the seized opium of the British and American firms in the open at the beach at Humen, more than 2.37 million catties of it; he reorganised the coastal defence, raised naval funds, and collected accounts of foreign geography and sea defences that later became the basis of Wei Yuan's Haiguo Tuzhi; in June 1840 he was dismissed and sent to Ili, so that he was already gone from Canton when the fighting began. The Governor-General of Liangguang Deng Tingzhen had the opium smokers executed at Huangpu in 1838, executed the destruction at Humen together with Lin Zexu, and died of illness the same year. Qishan was sent to Canton in January 1840 to negotiate; the terms he discussed included the cession of Hong Kong, he was rebuked by the Daoguang Emperor, was escorted to the capital in November, and died on the road in February of the following year. Yishan took over the Guangdong command at the end of 1840 and inflicted a severe defeat on the British at Chuenpi on 26 January 1841, only to be transferred away shortly afterwards. Among the defenders, Guan Tianpei died at the Humen forts, Chen Huacheng died at Amoy, Guo Yongsheng was killed at Sheqiao, Hailing killed himself after Zhenjiang fell, Chu Yupu surrendered Dinghai, and Yan Baozao drowned himself after the loss of Amoy, while a number of officers who had lost their positions were beheaded. The central figure on the British side was Charles Elliot, Superintendent of Trade in China: in March 1839 he wrote to Lin Zexu demanding the surrender of all the opium, and in November he ordered the merchant fleet to seize Chinese junks off Chuenpi, which opened the conflict; he was wounded at Chuenpi afterwards, was recalled, and was succeeded by Henry Pottinger, who in 1842 led the force up the Yangtze and signed the Treaty of Nanking on board HMS Cornwallis on 29 August. The army was commanded by the naval commander-in-chief Sir Hugh Gough, the squadron at Amoy was led by Sir Edward Codrington, and the young Charles Gordon came ashore with the 2nd Battalion of the Royal Marines at Zhenjiang and saw the worst night of the war.
kits: 卡面上這件法國雷管步槍，是法軍在十九世紀三四十年代把火燧槍改為雷管（擊發）機制後的制式步兵槍：一八三六年式把一八一四年式火槍改成雷管，一八四〇年前後仍在成批生產，其後就是法軍一八四四年式。它靠擊發機撞擊底火，底火是藥劑而非燧石與火藥，因此濕氣、霧氣、暴雨都不會像火繩槍那樣熄火，單兵裝填與射擊速度也更快；按法軍制式表，一八四四年式每營備彈約一千一百八十發，槍身連刺刀約五公斤出頭，而卡面那句射程變長、隊形就散，正是雷管槍帶來的射擊精度與有效射程提升在戰術上的代價。這件兵器本身沒有出現在本次戰爭的戰場上——法國在一八三九至一八四二年保持中立，沒有向中國派出遠征軍，法國的介入要等到一八五六年第二次鴉片戰爭。真正在珠江口與南京城下的，是同一技術世代的英軍武器：一八四二年制式步槍、重約四點五公斤、有效射程三百五十至五百碼的貝克萊槍、配在平底炮船上作近距抵射的二十四磅砲、三十二磅卡龍砲、少量康格里夫火箭，以及鐵殼蒸汽艦尼米西斯號。相對地，清軍的火力核心是虎門、吳淞各砲台的數十門大炮，其中數千斤重的舊式鑄炮射程雖遠卻精度低，輔以鳥槍、抬槍、劈山炮與師船上的中小型火炮，近岸火力密集而精度不足，並有攔江鐵索、縱火船與藤牌竹篙一類防禦器材。
kitsEn: The French percussion rifle on the card is the standard infantry arm the French army reached after converting flintlocks to the percussion, or striking, mechanism during the 1830s and 1840s: the Model 1836 converted the Model 1814 musket to percussion and was still being produced in batches around 1840, and was followed by the Model 1844. The hammer strikes a percussion cap, and because the priming is a chemical cap rather than flint and priming powder, damp, fog and heavy rain cannot put it out as they could a matchlock, and the rate of loading and firing by an individual soldier rises as well; by the French establishment table a battalion of Model 1844 muskets was issued with about 1,180 rounds, and the musket with bayonet weighed a little over five kilogrammes. The sentence on the card about longer range and formations coming apart is exactly the tactical price of the accuracy and effective range that the percussion musket brought. This weapon itself was not on the battlefield of this war: France stayed neutral between 1839 and 1842 and sent no expeditionary force to China, and French intervention did not come until the Second Opium War of 1856. What stood at the mouth of the Pearl River and below the walls of Nanjing belonged to the same technological generation on the British side: the Pattern 1842 Percussion Musket, the Baker rifle of about 4.5 kilogrammes with an effective range of three hundred and fifty to five hundred yards, the twenty-four-pounder guns carried on flat-bottomed gunboats for close bombardment, thirty-two-pounder carronades, a few Congreve rockets, and the iron-hulled steamer HMS Nemesis. On the Chinese side the core of firepower was the dozens of heavy guns in the Humen and Wusong forts, among them old cast bronze pieces of several thousand catties with long range but poor accuracy, supported by matchlock guns, gingals, small mortars and the medium and small guns of the war junks: dense coastal firepower, but not accurate firepower, and along with it chains stretched across the river, fire ships, and rattan shields and bamboo poles for pushing those fire ships out.
tactics: 英軍的整套打法是海軍先行、陸軍跟進的兩棲戰：先用分艦隊封鎖珠江口與閩浙沿海，切斷廣州與沿海各省的貿易與糧運，再用平底炮船與小型蒸汽船溯江逼近砲台，以船載二十四磅砲在數百碼內抵近射擊，把清軍岸防砲台逐個打啞。登陸一律用平底小艇分批偷渡，士兵在灘頭即成散兵線，用步槍齊射壓制守軍射界，再以刺刀和工兵逐段攻堡。步兵作戰仍是密集線形，射擊距離約二百至三百碼；步槍旅則以散兵線作戰，貝克萊槍的射程足以在清軍抬槍射程之外先發制人。一八四二年七月鎮江之戰，英軍在夜裡用舟船靠岸、以攀梯攀城，奪城後逐街巷清理守軍，最慘烈的一夜戰即出自此役。英軍的補給線拉得極長：兵員多自孟買、加爾各答調來，軍火由印度軍械庫發給，總部與後勤基地設在香港的維多利亞城，長江作戰時則靠艦隊沿途提供糧水與彈藥。清軍的戰術守舊而頑強：以數千斤大炮配泥牆與土壘構成封鎖線，虎門江面拉起攔江鐵索阻擋英船溯流，派師船與哨船巡邏，屢以縱火船衝撞敵艦，曾在穿鼻兩度逼近焚燒英船。守軍多奉死守之令，依托砲台與村落反覆反擊，不退者賞、潰退者斬，結果在若干戰敗指揮官被論斬之後，軍心與指揮體系都受重創；清廷屢次增調湖南、廣西兵源，仍趕不上英軍在兵種、射擊精度與後勤上的差距。
tacticsEn: The British method was a two-stage amphibious operation with the navy leading and the army following: the squadron first blockaded the mouth of the Pearl River and the coast of Fujian and Zhejiang, cutting the trade of Canton and the food supply of the coastal provinces, and then flat-bottomed gunboats and small steamers worked upstream to close on the forts, the ship-borne twenty-four-pounders firing at a few hundred yards to knock the shore batteries out one by one. Landings were made in flat-bottomed boats in small batches; the men formed skirmish lines as soon as they touched the beach, used musket volleys to dominate the defenders' field of fire, and then took the works section by section with the bayonet and the engineers. The infantry still fought in dense line, at two to three hundred yards, while the rifle brigade fought in extended order, the range of the Baker rifle allowing it to open fire beyond the reach of the Chinese gingals. At Zhenjiang in July 1842 the British brought their boats to the shore at night, scaled the walls, and cleared the defenders street by street, and the bloodiest night of the war came out of that action. The British line of supply was stretched to extraordinary length: the men were drawn largely from Bombay and Calcutta, the ammunition came out of the Indian arsenals, the headquarters and base of supply sat at Victoria in Hong Kong, and on the Yangtze the squadron supplied food, water and ammunition along the route. The Chinese method was obsolete but stubborn: a blocking line of several-thousand-cattied guns backed by mud walls and earthworks, chains drawn across the Humen channel to stop British ships from going upstream, war junks and fast scout boats on patrol, and repeated rushes at enemy ships with fire ships, which twice came close to burning British vessels at Chuenpi. The defenders were generally ordered to hold to the death, rallying from the batteries and the villages, and were rewarded for not retreating and punished for it, so that after a number of defeated commanders were executed both the morale of the troops and the command structure were badly shaken; the Qing court repeatedly drew in troops from Hunan and Guangxi, and still could not match the British advantage in arms, in accuracy of fire and in logistics.
data: 有根據可寫的數字大致如下。一八三九年虎門銷煙自五月六日至六月二十五日，前後二十三日，銷毀鴉片二百三十七萬三千八百四十二斤，約合一千二百公噸，出自英美商行者逾兩萬箱；在此之前，一八三八年中國輸入的印度鴉片估計達四萬箱上下，是當時中國最大的單一進口商品。英軍兵力方面，一八四〇年首批遠征軍約七千人，其中孟加拉印度部隊佔一兩千人；一八四一年秋自英格蘭出發的增援約九千人，於一八四二年四月抵達，至一八四二年在華英軍合計接近兩萬。一八四〇年一月七日穿鼻海戰，英方出動三艘帆船，旗艦七十四門，另有十四門與二十六門各一艘，參戰英印軍約一千人；清方以三四十艘師船與約三千至五千人應戰，英軍傷亡數十人，清軍陣亡數百，數字各家記載不一，實際戰果遠不如清廷奏報所稱。次年一月二十六日的穿鼻之戰方向相反：清軍在關天培、陳化成、楊芳等指揮下重創英軍，英方三個營及印度兵受挫，被迫退回香港。一八四一年八月二十六日廈門之戰，英方以七艘軍艦、約二千四百名陸戰隊與六門野戰砲、六門臼砲對上約三千至五千守軍，英軍陣亡僅十餘人，清軍折損數百至逾千，陳化成陣亡。一八四二年七月二十一日鎮江之戰，英軍投入約一千七百人、艦船七艘、火砲十二門，守軍約一千五百人，常見記載為清軍陣亡二百二十二人、受傷五百餘人、被俘約一千四百人。距離與時間方面，自英格蘭繞好望角至中國約一萬四千英里，合二萬二千五百公里上下；英軍沿長江由海口溯至南京，行程約一千一百公里。理賠金額為二千一百萬銀圓，分三年支付。
dataEn: The figures that can be given on good authority are roughly these. The destruction of the opium at Humen ran from 6 May to 25 June 1839, twenty-three days in all, and destroyed 2,373,842 catties of opium, about 1,200 tonnes, taken from more than twenty thousand chests belonging to the British and American firms; before that, the Indian opium imported into China in 1838 is estimated at some forty thousand chests, making it the largest single import the country took. On the British strength, the first expeditionary force of 1840 numbered about seven thousand men, of whom a thousand or two were Bengal troops; the reinforcements that sailed from England in the autumn of 1841 numbered about nine thousand and reached China in April 1842, and by 1842 the total British force in the country was close to twenty thousand. At the battle of Chuenpi on 7 January 1840 the British brought out three sailing warships, the flagship carrying seventy-four guns and the others fourteen and twenty-six, with about a thousand British and Indian troops; the Chinese answered with thirty or forty war junks and some three to five thousand men; the British losses were a few dozen and the Chinese dead numbered several hundred, though the accounts differ widely and the real result was far smaller than the Qing memorial claimed. The battle of Chuenpi on 26 January of the following year ran the other way: the Chinese under Guan Tianpei, Chen Huacheng and Yang Fangchen mauled the British, three battalions and the Indian troops being thrown back and forced to retire to Hong Kong. At the battle of Amoy on 26 August 1841 the British had seven warships, about 2,400 marines and soldiers, six field guns and six mortars against some three to five thousand defenders; the British lost only a dozen or so dead while the Chinese lost from several hundred to more than a thousand, Chen Huacheng among them. At the battle of Zhenjiang on 21 July 1842 the British committed about seventeen hundred men, seven ships and twelve guns against roughly fifteen hundred defenders, and the figures usually given are two hundred and twenty-two defenders killed, more than five hundred wounded and about fourteen hundred taken prisoner. As to distance and time, the passage from England round the Cape of Good Hope to China is about fourteen thousand miles, some twenty-two thousand five hundred kilometres; the British advance up the Yangtze from the sea to Nanjing was a journey of roughly eleven hundred kilometres of river. The indemnity was fixed at 2,100,000 silver dollars, payable over three years.
cause: 鴉片是這場戰爭的燃料，貿易失衡才是它的根。東印度公司壟斷印度鴉片生產，1833年壟斷期結束後，英資私人商行在孟加拉大量收購鴉片，經鴛鴦號走私船隊從印度運入廣州、廈門與寧波，以每箱數百銀圓的價錢售予中國商人，走私網路由十三行商號與地方官員分潤，規模在十九世紀三十年代急遽膨脹。鴉片賣掉，白銀流進英國，中國的銀兩卻大量外流，導致銀價下跌、財政吃緊，廣東、廣西兩省的地方稅收與民生首當其衝，朝廷因此把查禁鴉片列為要務。衝突由執法升級為開戰：道光十七年鄧廷楨在黃埔絞決吸食鴉片者，道光十八年林則徐到廣州，封閉十三行、斷絕中英貿易，一八三九年三月義律要求交出全部鴉片，林則徐以整批繳交為條件、且拒絕讓英國船隻進口，義律則以英商無權代交他人財產、且英船不進口即不得交貨為由拒絕，最終朝廷下令在虎門海灘全數銷毀。銷煙之後，廣州英商與清廷的摩擦並未停止，一八三九年八月發生英國旗事件，清方驅逐三艘英國商船、命令洋行商人不得與英人往來，英方隨即以武裝力量報復。十一月，義律令商人武裝船隊在穿鼻攔截中國運鹽帆船，雙方在虎門江口交火，清方出動師船與水師圍攻，事件擴大為第一次穿鼻海戰。深層次還有制度層面的衝突：英方要求以國家對國家方式通商，要求清朝按對等外交禮節接見有資格的使臣，清廷則堅持外國使臣只能走廣州一途、經十三行與粵海關官員接洽，兩套秩序無法並存。一八四〇年四月英國內閣拍板遠征，一八四二年戰爭結束。
causeEn: Opium was the fuel of this war, but the imbalance of trade was its root. The East India Company held a monopoly on the production of Indian opium, and when that monopoly lapsed in 1833, private British firms bought opium in great quantities in Bengal and ran it into Canton, Amoy and Ningbo by the opium fleet of country boats, selling it to Chinese merchants at several hundred silver dollars a chest, with the smuggling chain shared by the Hong merchants of the Thirteen Factories and by local officials, and growing at a furious rate through the 1830s. As opium was sold, silver flowed out of China into Britain, silver prices fell, the treasury tightened, and the revenue and the livelihoods of Guangdong and Guangxi suffered first, so the court made the suppression of opium a matter of state. The quarrel was escalated from enforcement into war: in 1838 Deng Tingzhen executed opium smokers at Huangpu, and in 1839 Lin Zexu arrived in Canton, closed the Thirteen Factories and cut off Sino-British trade. In March 1839 Elliot demanded the surrender of all the opium; Lin offered to hand it over in bulk and refused the ships' right of entry; Elliot answered that British merchants had no property in other people's opium to surrender and that without entry there could be no surrender. The court then ordered the whole quantity destroyed on the beach at Humen. The destruction did not end the friction between the British merchants in Canton and the Chinese authorities: in August 1839 came the affair of the British flag, the Chinese expelling three British trading ships and ordering the Hong merchants to have no intercourse with the English, and the British answered with armed force. In November Elliot ordered the merchant fleet, now armed, to intercept Chinese salt junks off Chuenpi; shots were exchanged at the Humen mouth, the Chinese sent out war junks and the navy to surround the attackers, and the incident grew into the first battle of Chuenpi. Beneath it lay a clash of systems: the British wanted commerce conducted between nation and nation and wanted the Qing court to receive an accredited envoy on terms of equal diplomatic courtesy, while the court insisted that foreign envoys could come only by the Canton route and be dealt with through the Thirteen Factories and the customs officials, and the two orders of things could not coexist. In April 1840 the British cabinet decided on the expedition, and in 1842 the war ended.
impact: 這場戰爭結束後的世界，秩序被重寫。對英國而言，廣州不再是唯一口岸，五口通商把中國市場推開一個口子，一八四二年後對華輸出品額迅速上升，英國商船第一次可以沿著長江直入內地，鴉片生意不但沒有收手，反而在五口通商與協議關稅之後更趨合法與膨脹，為一八五六年第二次鴉片戰爭埋下新的導火線。對中國而言，一八四二年《南京條約》與一八四三年的《虎門條約》以及一系列附約確立了近代中國不平等條約的樣板：割地香港島、賠款二千一百萬銀圓、協定關稅、最惠國待遇，隨後又在通商口岸推行領事裁判權，一部條約口岸體系由此成形，中國在法律上第一次被置於不平等地位。這也把近代東亞的國際秩序推向槍炮外交的時代：英國在中國沿海取得的示範效應，隨後用於對日本的強制外交以及對緬甸的推進。中國社會的反應分成兩條線：一條是林則徐、魏源《海國圖志》（一八四二年）、徐繼畬《瀛寰志略》（一八四八年）一類的經世之學，要求先認清西方；另一條是此後洋務派以師夷長技為口號引進西式船砲與船政（福州船政局、天津機器局），都以這場戰爭的恥感與教訓為起點。技術面的刺激同樣具體：鐵殼蒸汽船尼米西斯號在珠江上的出現，讓清廷第一次直觀看見蒸汽船對木殼帆船的世代差，之後洋務派造輪船、設船廠的動機正來自於此。
impactEn: After this war the order of the world was rewritten. For Britain, Canton was no longer the only port; the opening of five treaty ports pushed open a breach in the Chinese market, British exports to China rose quickly after 1842, and British ships for the first time could sail up the Yangtze into the interior. The opium trade did not stop; on the contrary, with the five ports and the agreed tariff it became more legitimate and larger, and it left a fresh fuse for the Second Opium War of 1856. For China, the Treaty of Nanking of 1842, the Treaty of the Bogue of 1843 and the supplementary agreements set the model for the unequal treaties of modern China: the cession of Hong Kong Island, an indemnity of 2,100,000 silver dollars, an agreed tariff and most-favoured-nation treatment, followed later by consular jurisdiction at the treaty ports. A treaty-port system was thereby formed, and China was for the first time placed in an unequal position under law. The war also pushed the modern East Asian order into the age of gunboat diplomacy: the demonstration the British had given on the Chinese coast was used afterwards in the coercive diplomacy pressed on Japan and in the British advance in Burma. Chinese society answered along two lines: one was the school of statecraft studies represented by Lin Zexu, by Wei Yuan's Haiguo Tuzhi of 1842 and by Xu Jiyu's Yinghuan Zhilue of 1848, which called for understanding the West before anything else; the other was the later self-strengthening programme, which under the slogan of learning the barbarians' superior arts introduced Western guns, ships and arsenals, the Fuzhou Dockyard and the Tientsin Arsenal, and which took its origin in the humiliation and the lesson of this war. The stimulus on the technological side was equally concrete: the sight of the iron-hulled steamer Nemesis in the Pearl River showed the Qing court for the first time with their own eyes the generation gap between a steamship and a wooden sailing ship, and it was from that shock that the later incentive to build steamships and found dockyards came.
result: 以一八四二年八月二十九日《南京條約》在南京江面上的英國旗艦康華利號上簽署為終點，結果是清廷在軍事上認敗而未亡國。條約的核心條件有數：割讓香港島並准英國在島上駐軍；開廣州、福州、廈門、寧波、上海五處為通商口岸，英國得派駐領事，官民可在口岸居住貿易；准許英國軍艦與商船在通商口岸及長江大河自由航行，並由中國供給淡水、糧秣與修理之便；中國割讓英國銀圓二千一百萬，分三年支付；通商口岸的稅則由中英共同議定，並援用最惠國待遇。附帶的《虎門條約》與五口通商章程，又補上領事裁判權與租地建屋的安排。軍事過程的關鍵節點也一併留在記錄裡：一八四〇年一月穿鼻海戰英方得手，同年七月英軍攻佔定海；一八四一年一月清軍在穿鼻反攻得手、二月虎門砲台失守、五月英軍再奪穿鼻、八月廈門失守、十月定海與寧波相繼淪陷、十二月英軍一度攻入鎮江；一八四二年英軍溯長江，六月直抵南京城下，雙方在城外三江營一帶交戰之後，清廷同意議和。戰爭沒有解決貿易上的真正爭端，鴉片禁令照舊，清廷的禁絕也照舊，雙方矛盾在十年之後再度爆發，導向一八五六年第二次鴉片戰爭。
resultEn: The war ended on 29 August 1842 with the signature of the Treaty of Nanking on board the British flagship HMS Cornwallis in the Yangtze above Nanjing, and the result was a military defeat for the Qing that did not cost them the state. The main terms were these: Hong Kong Island was ceded, and the British were allowed to station troops on it; Guangzhou, Fuzhou, Amoy, Ningbo and Shanghai were opened as treaty ports where the British might appoint consuls and where their officials and merchants might reside and trade; British warships and merchant ships were to be free to move among the ports and on the great rivers of the interior, and China was to supply them with water, food and the means of repair; China was to pay the British 2,100,000 silver dollars over three years; the tariff at the treaty ports was to be fixed by agreement between the two states, and the most-favoured-nation clause was to apply. The accompanying Treaty of the Bogue and the regulations for the five ports added consular jurisdiction and the arrangements for leasing and building on the foreign quarter. The military milestones remain on the record as well: the British won the battle of Chuenpi in January 1840 and took Dinghai that July; the Chinese counter-stroke at Chuenpi succeeded in January 1841, the Humen forts fell in February, the British retook Chuenpi in May, Amoy was lost in August, Dinghai and Ningbo fell in October one after the other, and the British entered Zhenjiang in December; in 1842 the British went up the Yangtze, reached Nanjing in June, fought around the Sanjiangying outside the walls, and the court then consented to negotiate. The war settled none of the real trade grievance: the prohibition on opium remained in force on the Chinese side, and the two sides were still at odds a decade later, when the quarrel flared again into the Second Opium War of 1856.
